ManagerPayPage.sousTitre: You are paid a CPM on the views of the videos assigned to the creators you manage.
ManagerPayPage.pasManager: This screen is for managers only: it shows their CPM earnings.
ManagerPayPage.aucunCpm: No CPM has been set for you on this project yet. As soon as a rate is set for a creator, their views and your earnings will show up here.

ManagerPayReport.aucuneVideo: No published video in this period.
ManagerPayReport.explication: Basis: the paid views of published videos (unpaid warm-up posts excluded, views counted over the 30-day pay window), multiplied by the CPM in effect on each video's publication date: a rate change only applies to videos published afterwards. The month is the video's publication month; a recent month keeps growing as long as its videos get views.
ManagerPayReport.confirmCorps: The payment to {manager} is recorded as is: it's what's left to pay for this month right now.
ManagerPayReport.confirmMoisOuvert: This month can still gain views (30-day window): the difference will then show up as “left to pay”.
ManagerPayReport.annulerCorps: The month becomes due again for the cancelled amount. The payment stays in the history, struck through.
ManagerPayReport.explicationVersements: “Mark as paid” records a payment of what's left to pay. If the videos of a month already paid keep getting views, the difference shows up again as “left to pay”.

VideoBonusEditor.cumulativeOn: A video earns the sum of every threshold it has crossed.
VideoBonusEditor.cumulativeOff: A video only earns the bonus of the highest threshold it has crossed.
VideoBonusEditor.pivotSingle: A video at {views} views earns {amount} — with a single threshold, stacking makes no difference.
VideoBonusEditor.footnote: Views counted: those of paid promo posts, all platforms combined, within the video's pay window. The bonus is added on top of the fixed fee and CPM, outside the per-video cap.

transfers.title: Whop → bank withdrawals
transfers.subtitle: Say what each withdrawal was for, or split it into several parts. Only a part “counted as an expense” changes the result.
transfers.returned: Returned to Whop on {date}, not counted
transfers.failedNote: {count, plural, one {# failed, not counted} other {# failed, not counted}} ({list})
transfers.dialogIntro: Split the withdrawal into parts: each one says what the money was for. A business expense paid with it (ads, a tool, scans…) can be counted as an expense: it joins the month's expenses and lowers the result. The rest doesn't change the result: it's your money, it just leaves Whop.
transfers.effectScansHint: → counts in Scanning, instead of the {month} estimate
transfers.similarNone: no similar expense already entered in {month}
transfers.similarFound: An expense “{label}” of {amount} already exists in {month}: make sure it isn't the same one.
transfers.neverCounted: A “Creator payments” part is never counted: pay is already in Creators once you mark the cycle paid.
transfers.effectNone: No effect on the result: nothing is counted as an expense.
transfers.effectUnchanged: Withdrawals received, Whop net, gross revenue: unchanged
transfers.noteRequired: A note is required for a part counted as an expense
transfers.effectScansLow: {month} scanning drops by {amount}: a single counted payment replaces the whole estimate. If other scanning payments this month aren't counted yet (other withdrawals, card…), count them too, or the result is inflated.
transfers.recoverHint: Flagged at the top of Accounting until the usage changes. Recovered → “Other”; lost → “Business expenses”, counted.

charges.title: Other expenses
charges.subtitle: Entered by hand, or counted from a split withdrawal: hosting, tools, subscriptions, advertising. Amount including tax, in the invoice currency, converted at the project rate.
charges.label: Label
charges.footer: An “every month” expense is planned on the same day of the following months: confirm it (or correct it), or stop the series. A payment to the scan provider goes under Scanning: it replaces the month's estimate.
charges.noCurrency: Set the project's rates first: without a reference currency, an expense can't be converted.
charges.waitingImport: Expenses can be entered after the first Whop ledger import: it sets the reference currency.
charges.stopped: Series stopped: no more planned expenses.
charges.dialogDescription: Amount including tax, as it appears on the invoice.
charges.monthlyHint: Planned on the same day of the following months, to confirm.
charges.scanWarning: A payment to the scan provider goes under Scanning: it counts in the Scanning column, instead of the month's estimate.
charges.deleteBody: The expense disappears from the month and from the export.
charges.deleteSeries: This is the last expense of an “every month” series: the series stops too.

method.source: Source: GET /financial_activity from the Whop API (the account ledger), one line per money movement. Each line type (line_type) goes into a single column. An unknown type is never ignored: it stays “unclassified” until you file it.
method.refunds: Money given back to customers, including resolution center refunds; a reversed refund comes back as positive.
method.disputes: Disputed amounts; a dispute won comes back as positive.
method.fees: Every type ending in _fee (and its _fee_reversal): processing, foreign card, currency exchange, dispute, withdrawal…
method.transfers: Money leaving the Whop balance for the bank account: cash, outside the result. Purpose and split are yours; only a part counted as an expense enters the result. A failed withdrawal, returned to Whop, doesn't count.
method.internal: Reserves and internal conversions: they move money, they don't create any.
method.userRulesHint: types Whop sends that Jarvia didn't know
method.pendingAction: {count, plural, one {Classify # pending type} other {Classify # pending types}}
method.rulesFoot: A rule files every line of its type, past and future. Removing it sends those lines back to “unclassified”. Types Jarvia already knows, listed above, can't be changed here.
method.removeBody: Its lines go back to “unclassified” and leave their column.
method.removeExported: Months already exported that would change: {months}.
method.formula: Whop net = gross revenue − refunds − disputes − fees. Creators = cycles marked paid and partial payments, on the day they were sent. Scanning = real payments to the provider (Scanning category) when there are any, otherwise the app's cost_usd estimate, every scan included, locked two days after the month ends. Other expenses = entered by hand or counted from a withdrawal.
method.differs: Figures may differ from the Analytics tab: accounting reads the full ledger, internal subscriptions included, while Analytics reads payments excluding internal accounts.

classify.title: File unknown Whop lines
classify.description: Pick a column for each type. Your choice becomes a rule: every line of that type, past and future, goes into that column.
classify.effectNet: {amount} into “{bucket}”: Whop net and the result move by the same amount.
classify.effectGross: Also counts in gross revenue to date, so against the thresholds.
classify.effectTransfers: {amount} into “Withdrawals received”: cash, the result doesn't move.
classify.effectInternal: {amount} outside the result: neither the net nor the result moves.
classify.exported: Already exported: {months}. The export for those months would change, redo it afterwards.
classify.internalHint: “Outside the result” = an internal movement, or money already counted elsewhere (a creator paid through Whop is already in Creators once you mark her cycle paid).
classify.saved: {count, plural, one {Rule saved.} other {# rules saved.}}

exportDialog.title: Export for the accountant
exportDialog.description: One file per month that opens as-is in Excel set to French: “;” separator, decimal comma, DD/MM/YYYY dates.
exportDialog.journalNote: Each amount keeps its original currency, the rate and its converted value. Whop references (pay_, wdrl_) to find a line.
exportDialog.summaryNote: Recomputed from the same journal: the two files can't contradict each other.
exportDialog.incomplete: This month has amounts that couldn't be valued (currency without a rate, scans without a cost): their cells stay empty, never zero.
exportDialog.unclassified: {count, plural, one {# unclassified line} other {# unclassified lines}}: they appear in the journal under “Unclassified”.
exportDialog.scanPaidLow: Scanning: actual ({paid}) is far below the estimate ({estimate}). A payment may be missing: check before sending.
exportDialog.creatorsGap: Creators: {sent} sent from Whop for them vs {paid} marked paid (gap {gap}). Clear it up before sending.
